name: LLM Superagent
description: An autonomous team for any LLM: your agent routes each request into a ticket and hands it to a worker sub-agent (code, research, analysis, review, docs) on the model from your list best suited to its type of task and requirements.
author: eskwisit

en.name: LLM Superagent
en.description: An autonomous team for any LLM: your agent routes each request into a ticket and hands it to a worker sub-agent (code, research, analysis, review, docs) on the model from your list best suited to its type of task and requirements.
en.safetyNotes: Agent tools plus a skill; no network access and no process execution. agent.prompt.inject indexes the LLM Superagent skill for the Skill tool. agent.tool.register adds one gateway tool at load (superagent) which, on its first call, registers the seven tools the orchestrating agent calls (superagent_config, superagent_models, superagent_intake, superagent_route, superagent_eval_decide, superagent_reply, superagent_ticket), so idle sessions carry one tool entry. models.list reads which of your signed-in models you enabled for sub-agents (never any key) to pick each worker's model. fs.read and fs.write are scoped to .superagent/** in the workspace, where the team keeps its state, worker briefs and reports. Beyond the host file API the plugin uses Node fs only to copy its five worker-*.md sub-agents to ~/.agents/subagents when the gateway is first called in a session and after a settings change, with the thinking level that excludeThinking allows (the only place PI-Desktop loads sub-agents from), remove them on unload unless you edited them, and read its own default team sections. Workers are ordinary PI-Desktop sub-agents: the code and docs workers can edit workspace files, and every worker can run shell commands, with the permissions PI-Desktop grants sub-agents. Workers that change files run in parallel, each in its own git worktree under .superagent/worktrees on a local superagent/<ticket> branch; a merge worker then lands the branches in your checkout as uncommitted changes. Without git they run one at a time. The policy, role models, trait overrides, exclusions, notes, slots and team sections are plugin settings.

zh-CN.name: LLM 超级智能体
zh-CN.description: 适用于任何大模型的自主团队：你的智能体把每个请求转为一张工单，交给一个工作子智能体（代码、调研、分析、审查、文档），并从你的模型列表中挑选最适合该任务类型和要求的模型来运行。
zh-CN.safetyNotes: 智能体工具加一个技能；不访问网络，插件本身不运行任何进程。agent.prompt.inject 用于为 Skill 工具索引 LLM 超级智能体技能。agent.tool.register 在加载时只注册一个入口工具（superagent），首次调用时再注册七个由编排智能体调用的工具（superagent_config、superagent_models、superagent_intake、superagent_route、superagent_eval_decide、superagent_reply、superagent_ticket）。models.list 读取你在已登录的模型中启用给子智能体的那些模型（从不读取任何密钥），用于为每个工作者挑选模型。fs.read 与 fs.write 仅限工作区中的 .superagent/**，团队在其中保存状态、工作简报和报告。在宿主文件 API 之外，插件仅用 Node fs 做以下事情：会话中首次调用工具时及设置变更后将五个 worker-*.md 子智能体复制到 ~/.agents/subagents，并写入 excludeThinking 允许的思考级别（PI-Desktop 唯一加载子智能体的位置），卸载时删除它们（你修改过的除外），以及读取插件自带的默认团队章节。工作者是普通的 PI-Desktop 子智能体：代码和文档工作者可以编辑工作区文件，所有工作者都可以运行 shell 命令，权限与 PI-Desktop 授予子智能体的相同。修改文件的工作者并行运行，各自在 .superagent/worktrees 下自己的 git 工作树中、在本地 superagent/<工单> 分支上工作；随后由合并工作者把这些分支作为未提交的更改合入你的检出目录。没有 git 时，它们一次只运行一个。策略、角色模型、特性覆盖、排除项、备注、并发数和团队章节均保存在插件设置中。

agentTools.name: superagent
agentTools.description: LLM Superagent gateway: call first, only from the llm-superagent skill.

agentTools.name: superagent_config
agentTools.description: LLM Superagent: get or set policy, slots, role models, model traits, exclusions, team sections; lists sub-agent models. Only from the llm-superagent skill.

mode.description: set: accept mode for proactive (inferred) candidates

allowed.description: set: sender ids allowed to request work (default ["person"])

admission.description: set: { listedUnaddressed: inferred|ignore, unlistedAddressed: explicit|inferred|ignore, unlistedUnaddressed: inferred|ignore }

proofRounds.description: set: failed proof rounds before the person decides, 0–6 (default 3); 0 turns checks off

evalTimeoutSeconds.description: set: seconds a candidate waits for a decision, 30–3600 (default 120)

paused.description: set: pause processing; messages are still recorded

isolation.description: set: writers in git worktrees once git is confirmed (auto, default), from the start (worktree), or one at a time (serial)

roleModels.description: set: { taskType: [model, fallback, …] }; [] removes a pin

profiles.description: set: { glob: { reasoning|coding|writing|context|speed|cost: 1-5, vision|reasoningModel|unstable: bool, thinking: [levels] } }; null removes

exclude.description: set: model id globs never to use

excludeThinking.description: set: thinking levels workers never get (default ["high", "xhigh", "max"]; [] allows all)

team.description: set: { communication|scope|delivery: text }; "" restores the default

show.description: get: team sections to return in full

clear.description: set: reset role models, overrides, exclusions and notes first

agentTools.name: superagent_models
agentTools.description: LLM Superagent: preview the model, fallbacks and thinking level a task type and requirements get. Only from the llm-superagent skill.

requirements.description: optional: quality low|normal|high|max, speed low|normal|high, budget low|normal|high, context short|normal|long|huge, vision bool, reasoning bool, thinking level, differentFrom [ticket ids], prefer [globs], avoid [globs]

explain.description: also return the top 5 candidates with scores

agentTools.name: superagent_intake
agentTools.description: LLM Superagent: record a person's message verbatim; a thread reply goes to that ticket's worker, anything else returns a candidate card. Only from the llm-superagent skill.

addressed.description: false for shared material, an aside or thinking aloud; default true

thread.description: only when the message replies within an existing thread: its key

agentTools.name: superagent_route
agentTools.description: LLM Superagent: decide explicit candidate cards: accept (one ticket, or tickets[] per named part), attach, stop or ignore; items are independent. Only from the llm-superagent skill.

trigger_id.description: the card's trigger_id (a follow-up's for stop)

reason.description: ignore and stop: why, at most 500 characters

title.description: accept: short label of the request, ≤200 chars

name.description: accept: short English name, becomes the ticket id

acknowledgement.description: accept: one sentence in the person's language naming the concrete change and result, ≤100 words

note.description: optional: routing background or a limit the person stated, ≤30 words; never instructions

type.description: accept: picks the worker and its model

requirements.description: optional: quality low|normal|high|max, speed low|normal|high, budget low|normal|high, context short|normal|long|huge, vision bool, reasoning bool, thinking level, differentFrom [ticket ids], prefer [globs], avoid [globs]

scope.description: accept: one sentence naming the work allowed; defaults to the title

check.description: accept: check before merge. full: acceptance tests + proof on another model; proof: proof only; none: trivial change. Default full (code, debug), proof (test), none (docs)

repo.description: accept: optional project folder (own git repo inside a multi-project workspace), relative to the workspace root; omit when the root is the repo

tickets.description: accept: one entry per part the message names (2–8), run in parallel unless after; the item's acknowledgement covers all

name.description: accept: short English name, becomes the ticket id

note.description: optional: routing background or a limit the person stated, ≤30 words; never instructions

after.description: optional: names of entries whose results this one needs; it starts once they ended

agentTools.description: LLM Superagent: judge an inferred candidate against every enabled rule; accept creates a ticket only in auto mode with a settled direction. Only from the llm-superagent skill.

rule_assessments.description: Exactly one entry per enabled rule

intent_evidence.description: accept: the three facts (this project, change wanted, direction settled) with quotes

agentTools.name: superagent_reply
agentTools.description: LLM Superagent: clear a message to the person before posting: result, attention (the ticket's question, exact) or answer; ≤100 words, never twice. Only from the llm-superagent skill.

agentTools.name: superagent_ticket
agentTools.description: LLM Superagent: list, read, report (a returned worker turn), retry, recover, status, note, unsubscribe, requeue, dismiss, merge. Only from the llm-superagent skill.

turn.description: report: the turn number that returned

attempt.description: report: the launch item's attempt number

outcome.description: report: returned, or failed (error, timeout, limit)

failures.description: report: every `Model … failed (…)` line of the Task result, verbatim, even when the worker then returned

text.description: report: the sub-agent's reply (fallback when no report file). note: one fact, ≤100 words

model.description: retry: run on this model instead

settings.title: Policy
settings.description: Accept mode (off, observe, auto), rules for proactive work, allowed senders and admission. Edit through the agent (superagent_config) rather than by hand.

settings.title: Concurrent workers
settings.description: Worker turns running at once (1–8); one extra slot is kept for your messages.

settings.title: Proof rounds
settings.description: Checked code and debug tickets get acceptance tests written in parallel and a proof by another model, which sends defects back to the worker until the work passes. This is how many proof rounds may fail before you decide (0–6); 0 turns checks off.

settings.title: Eval timeout (seconds)
settings.description: How long a candidate waits for a decision before it is queued again (30–3600).

settings.title: Paused
settings.description: Pause processing: messages are recorded, nothing is evaluated, launched or sent.

settings.title: Isolation of workers that change files
settings.description: auto: each code or docs worker works in its own git worktree once git is found in the workspace or the ticket's repo folder, and a merge worker lands the branches in your checkout; one at a time before that or without git. worktree: worktrees from the start. serial: one at a time in your checkout.

settings.title: Role models
settings.description: Models pinned per task type, { type: [model, fallback, …] }. Types: code, debug, test, research, analysis, review, docs, and the internal merge, spec (acceptance tests) and proof. Empty means picked automatically from your list.

settings.title: Model trait overrides
settings.description: Corrections to inferred model traits, { glob: { reasoning|coding|writing|context|speed|cost: 1-5, vision: bool } }.

settings.title: Excluded models
settings.description: Glob patterns of model ids never used, e.g. ["*preview*"].

settings.title: Excluded thinking levels
settings.description: Thinking levels workers never get, e.g. ["high", "xhigh", "max"]. A higher wanted level goes down to the next allowed one. [] allows all.

settings.title: Model notes
settings.description: Notes the orchestrator reads before routing, e.g. why a model is excluded.

settings.title: Team section: Communication
settings.description: Replaces the default Communication section every worker reads. Empty uses the default.

settings.title: Team section: Ticket scope
settings.description: Replaces the default Ticket scope section. Empty uses the default.

settings.title: Team section: Delivery requirements
settings.description: Replaces the default Delivery requirements section. Empty uses the default.

settings.title: Prompt revision
settings.description: Counts saves of the team sections; each brief records the revision it was written under.
